title: Orchestrated canary traffic controller for hosted API rollout hardening
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Harden the hosted API deployment pipeline by adding an orchestrated canary traffic controller that manages percent-based traffic ramps across regions, enforces rollout gates tied to LTS/version channels, and automates safe rollbacks. Scope: control-plane orchestration (traffic controller service + API), integration with smart routing for regional shard awareness, health and SLO gating (latency P95, error-rate, tail CPU GPU saturation), and operational tooling (dashboards, runbooks, PR automation). Success criteria: 1) reduce human intervention during multi-region rollouts by 80%, 2) detect and abort bad rollouts within 3 minutes of SLO breach, 3) support per-customer pinned versions and immediate safe fallback, 4) end-to-end tests and canary simulations in CI to prevent regressions.
decisions: Controller implemented as a small control-plane service (Go) that drives traffic via weighted routing APIs (Envoy xDS / gateway) rather than in-band changes to serving mesh
Use percent-based canary ramps with configurable windows (default 1m, 5m, 10m) and pause gates evaluated by telemetry (P95 latency, 5xx rate, GPU util).

Treat LTS channels as explicit rollout targets: channel name + pinned version mapping in config store; new versions go to 'edge' channel then promoted to 'stable' and 'lts' via manual/automated policies
Automated rollback criteria: breach of any gate for two consecutive windows or a single critical customer error event triggers immediate rollback and traffic shift to previous stable variant.
tradeoffs: Centralized controller reduces ad-hoc scripts but adds an availability dependency — mitigated via HA controller (leader election) and read-only fallback by routing layer.
Conservative ramping (slower ramps) reduces blast radius but increases time-to-fully-deployed for urgent fixes; we expose an emergency fast-path with SRE approval.
Relying on Envoy xDS increases complexity of config reconciliation vs. feature-flag based routing; chosen for fine-grained per-route weights and regional affinity.
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after postmortem for incident INC-2026-02-14 (regional rollout caused 30% error spike). Assigned to Marco.
2026-02-27: Design review with PM (Lena Morales) and SRE. Agreed on controller API schema and primary gates. Action: design doc (see Confluence).
2026-03-04: Prototype controller with Envoy xDS integration completed. End-to-end test harness for simulated traffic ramps added to CI (PR 5718).
2026-03-09: First staging canary run: detected regression in KV-cache warm-up causing P95 latency spike; added KV warm-up step to ramp plan (deferred full rollout).
2026-03-13: Iteration: implemented dual-gate check (latency + GPU-saturated-tail) and added dashboard panels for per-region ramp state. Preparing PR for controller HA and playbook.
notes: Follow-up action from INC-2026-02-14: regional rollout coordination was manual and lacked gate automation.
We will add a compatibility check for model variant kernel selection to the rollout pre-flight to avoid mismatched quantization paths during ramp.
Design includes a simulation mode: synthetic traffic + fault injection to validate rollback triggers in CI before any prod campaign.
